content.title: Kraken (2026) ⭐ 5.3 | Action, Thriller
content.text: Videos2Featured reviewsRisen from the depths of Norway's deepest fjord...Do you know the blissful feeling when small things that you love, but that have little or nothing in common with each other, come together? You should really cherish those moments! My favorite kind of horror movies are creature features with giant animals, especially sea creatures. I love the Scandinavian nature, and preferably the Norwegian Fjords. I love black metal, and the rather unknown - but great - band Vreid worked on the soundtrack. The fact that these three things come together in one movie made "Kraken" a must-see for me. Moreover, but this is very personal, I love my family and exceptionally they all came along when "Kraken" premiered at the Brussels' International Fantastic Film Festival.All that joy, and yet I only gave a 6/10 rating? Well, that's simply because "Kraken" is not a great movie. It was great fun to wacht, but I can't pretend it's the best movie of its type since the original "Jaws". At a fish farm in a remote village near Norway's deepest fjord, risky experiments are carried out with sonar systems and underwater sound waves. The experiments are supposed to improve the quality of the salmon, but they are causing massive fish deaths and the vibrations have apparently also awakened a gigantic monster from the depths. Director Pål Øie follows the traditional "nature goes bonkers" pattern: some tourists disappear, rebellious environmentalists spread incriminating material via social media, a marine biologist - who happens to be from the village - is sent in, and the mystery continues to expand until suddenly gigantic tentacles emerge from the water.The first half is too slow and patiently takes its time to show all the predictable/derivative situations as if they are featuring here for the first time in film history. We have the reunion with the childhood sweetheart, an extra dangerous demonstration of the sonars for the Japanese investors, the old fisherman telling the legend of the monster in the fjord, etc. Etc. The second half contains enough action and tension, but the horror and bloodshed on display remains limited. You can perfectly predict who survives and who doesn't, and we don't get to see much more than tentacles (with large suction cups) and a monstrous eye. And yet, if you're in the mood for a traditional "giant animal" horror movie, "Kraken" is worth it!Not worth it, disappointingI expected a lot. Maybe too much. Lots of Norwegian movies are good, and I was excited to see a movie revolving around kraken.It felt like the movie was in slow motion at some points. If you're not a fan of ai I wouldn't watch it, as some of the effects are clearly Ai-generated. The story was all over the place, it barely felt like it was about the kraken! When characters died I didn't feel anything, because we don't learn anything about them.In conclusion, slow and all over the place. The movie was less of a monster/legend-become-real movie and more of a low-budget, filmed in all one night YouTube movie.Blurred backgrounds - The MovieI really wanted to like this movie. I love monstermovies and especially those involving huge sea creatures. However, the actors, especially the main lead, were flat and boring. The script is riddled with crimes against physics, logic and common sense. The special effects are dubius and mostly hidden in blurred backgrounds - and OH MY GOD - the blurred backgrounds! Did you want to have a look at the fjord or the Kraken? Good luck, they will mostly be out of focus in the background. The sad face of an actor was often the only thing to look at, because everything else was blurred.I live in Oslo and cheered when I saw the blurred outline of our Opera House, just to realise that the blurred outline was the only thing I was allowed to see from my home city. All the effects seemed fake, there was no proper interaction between the effects and the actors - so the vast majority felt like CGI inserts. Look at a movie like Jurassic Park and the scene where the T-Rex blows Grant's hat off, to see how CGI and practical effects must co-exist in order to build an illusion.There was several deaths and other newsworthy stuff going on for quite some time wihtout any media attention and no other police presence than a single woman. How? Where are the journalists, the extra police, the crime scene investigators?Great monster movieThis is a great monster movie with references to shark attack, Jurassic park, Alien and others. Sure, it has its minor downsides like a deadbeat cop and many people surviving, but all in all a good movie. My partner gave it a 8 and my son gave it a 10. I ended up on a 9 here myself. It smells like at least one or two movies will come after Kraken 1.This film cured my crippling insomniaDespite being only 90 minutes long the film feels painfully slow. This is because we as the audience know exactly what's going on in the fjord, while for most of the runtime none of the characters do. This makes it impossible to relate to them, especially since almost every character in this film has no personality or charisma to make up for it.We have to slog through a lot of meaningless scenes that are clearly just filler. When we finally get to what we've been waiting for, it's underwhelming at best! And it doesn't last long compared to the rest of the movie.The film had potential with its theme, but it loses all credibility when the main character becomes a hypocrite while attempting to save the day.This film might have one redeeming quality tho; once it's available on streaming you can use it as a substitute for sleeping pills. For that, i have given the film 2/10 stars instead of just 1.More like thisRelated interestsJohanne is a marine biologist who is doing research on a fish farm in Vangsnes, a rural community located by the fjord, when she encounters several strange occurrences. Along with the brutal deaths of two local teenagers, all signs are pointing to the deep fjord; can there be more to the depths than the eye can see? At the bottom of Norway's deepest fjord rests a mythical monster as large as a mountain, with a myriad of arms ready to crush and devour anything they can grab.Plot summaryAdd synopsisContribute to this pageSuggest an edit or add missing contentEdit page
